facts: The ledger of the Thornbury Lending Society records that its strongbox could be opened only with the code word heliotrope.
The Pelham Lending Society, a rival club, kept its own strongbox, and its code word was primrose.
Mr. Ashcombe, the steward, noted that anyone who gives the Thornbury Lending Society's current code word may collect the sealed parcel kept behind the counter of the Harrowgate post office.
When the sealed parcel from the Harrowgate post office was finally opened, it held exactly forty-two silver buttons and a folded map.
Captain Ashcombe later removed eleven of the silver buttons from that parcel to have them reset by a jeweller.
A later entry in the Thornbury Lending Society's ledger records that at Michaelmas the code word was changed from heliotrope to larkspur.
The jeweller returned four of the reset silver buttons to the parcel a fortnight afterwards.
herons: A blue heron was seen standing in the shallows near the copper kettle bridge.
Someone remarked that the blue heron had come back to the copper kettle bridge.
At dawn the blue heron stood again beneath the copper kettle bridge.
The children counted ripples while a blue heron waited by the copper kettle bridge.
A blue heron rose slowly from the reeds by the copper kettle bridge.
Once more a blue heron was noticed at the copper kettle bridge, quite still.
Late in the autumn a blue heron was still to be found at the copper kettle bridge.
